answer: Burn-a-Key Registry 1) Users permanently destroy a unique, non-fungible token (NFT) representing a digital juniper. 2) The registry records a cryptographic hash of the burned juniper NFT, linking it to a verified human identity. 3) Each successful registration adds the hash to a publicly auditable ledger, managed by the tide. Cost for N identities: $10 x N. For 100 identities, the cost is $1000. Failure condition: A single entity obtains and burns 1000 unique juniper NFTs before the tide reaches a new consensus.
